title: Add restrained haptic feedback to shopping gestures
acceptance: 2026-11-20: user confirms haptics are good after testing the latest held-swipe refinement. Commit requested with the subsequent focus-fix closure.
requested: Cue at the mode-pull threshold, rather than at mode completion.
Cue as a horizontal check/uncheck/delete swipe starts; repeat within a held touch only when the row crosses its resting centre into the opposite action. Same-side pullback stays silent.
Cue when a long press pops a row out and on each normal drop.
Cue when the movable editor reaches a position selected by tapping.

recommendation.requested_actions: Confirm for mode-pull threshold crossings, shopping-mode check/uncheck and edit-mode deletion. Edit-mode check/uncheck retain ToggleOn/ToggleOff. DragStart marks row pickup; GestureEnd marks normal drops and editor arrival. Respect system Touch feedback.
additional_candidates: Undo confirmation remains proposed, not connected.
recommendation.avoid: No continuous buzzing or duplicate completion pulse. A recognized swipe or armed pull can have its initial cue even if the gesture is later pulled back/cancelled; cancellation adds no drop cue. No startup/reload/ordinary scrolling/typing/countdown feedback.

technical_review: For Qt 6.12 Android, use a small Qt/JNI bridge to the native View haptic-feedback API on Android's UI thread. Android recommends this semantic API: it requires no VIBRATE permission and respects system feedback settings. The user's linked XrHapticFeedback controls XR controllers. Qt supports Android-based OpenXR headsets such as Meta Quest; that is not the phone's built-in vibrator. Reuse existing Qt Core/Android support and existing AndroidX compatibility facilities where useful; do not add an XR module or haptic framework.
constraints: Preserve gesture thresholds, pullback, ordering, animations and continuous input. Respect system settings and older-API fallbacks. Emit once at the user-selected stage: threshold/swipe start, pickup/drop, editor arrival or real bulk deletion. Started-but-cancelled gestures may already have their initial cue; cancellation must not add a drop/completion cue. Unsupported/desktop systems retain full visual behavior.
verification_plan: Test action-to-effect dispatch through real gestures, Undo and pickup, including rejection, cancellation, duplicate signals and reload/no-op paths. Verify Android UI-thread/API fallback behavior, settings and package permissions/dependencies. A physical phone is required to judge feel and intensity; emulator dispatch tests cannot certify tactile quality.
scope: Requested effect mapping, repeated pulley threshold cues, held-swipe opposite-action cues and dragged-row index ticks are implemented and accepted on phone.

binding.api: Haptics.play(Confirm / ToggleOn / ToggleOff / DragStart / GestureEnd / SegmentTick), with requested(Feedback) observing request intent. Android dispatch is asynchronous; desktop has no device vibration.
binding.android: Resolve the current Activity/window/decor View on the Android UI thread; ignore inactive app, unavailable Activity/window and hidden/unfocused window. AndroidX ViewCompat performs the requested semantic feedback with older-API fallbacks and normal system-setting behavior. No VIBRATE permission or additional dependency.
binding.release: The actual R8 output DEX retains both JNI class names, performHapticFeedback(View,int), and all six constant fields including SEGMENT_TICK: out/ux008/index-tick-r8-retained.txt. No new runtime dependency or permission. This checks the Java boundary, not a complete Release artifact.
binding.verification: Accepted haptics ARM64 Debug APK includes repeated opposite-action cues within one held swipe. Payload/dependency closure, 21 Maven notices and all 96 source-input checks pass. Hash: out/ux008/held-swipes-arm64-hash.json; build: held-swipes-arm64-package.txt. Prior x86/native run evidence remains historical; no agent phone installation.
binding.limits: User accepted the latest haptics on phone. API-28 fallback behavior remains unverified. Earlier native emulator evidence covers the first five effects; SEGMENT_TICK is compiled against packaged AndroidX 1.17, its constant/API checked and its actual R8 retention verified. Undo feedback remains proposed.

integration.mode: 2026-11-20 refinement: Confirm on every below-to-above threshold crossing while an enabled, visible pulley is being dragged. Pulling back below re-arms immediately within the same drag. Staying above, crossing downward, releasing, later mode completion and Back mode exit add no cue. The per-drag latch and drag-start callback were removed.
integration.check: 2026-11-20: initial cue at horizontal recognition, then each crossing of the resting centre into the opposite action within the same held touch. Reversing while still on the same side stays silent. Shopping-mode check-in/out uses Confirm in either direction/state; edit-mode left check/uncheck retains ToggleOn/ToggleOff and right-delete Confirm. No duplicate completion cue.
integration.delete: Firmer Confirm at recognized right-swipe start in edit mode. Model.deletionRecorded confirms genuine bulk removals, including a hidden pending edit, with a scoped deletingBySwipe guard preventing a second swipe cue. Empty/read-only no-ops stay silent.
integration.reorder: 2026-11-20: DragStart on pickup, SegmentTick for each logical index change of the actively held row, GestureEnd on normal drop. TextDelegate emits reordered only while its long-press move is active. Other rows can change index or animate due to displacement but stay silent; cancellation adds no drop cue.
integration.editor: Explicitly requested: GestureEnd when the editor finishes its move to a position selected by a single tap. Track the actual editor delegate through the ListView move transition. Same-position taps and automatic model movement stay silent.
integration.timing: Gesture thresholds, list order and visual animations remain unchanged. These cues acknowledge arming/start/arrival rather than serving as proof of final list mutation.

verification.before: With the approved binding and request observer but no UI hookups, eight actual-control flow cases fail their requested-count assertions (0 versus expected 1/3); the complete baseline run then hits its 120-second timeout. This is not a completed full baseline suite: out/ux008/flows-before.txt.
verification.windows: Final flow suite: 20 records pass, including held threshold crossing, pullback/re-crossing once per pull, pickup/drop, editor travel versus arrival, same-position silence, and pending-only-row bulk deletion with Undo. Keyboard 14, recognized-swipe 24 and activated-window cancellation 11 records pass. Model 105 passed earlier with unchanged model code. Reports under out/ux008: refined-flow-final.txt, refined-flow-keyboard.txt, refined-swipes-final.txt and refined-cancellation.txt. Full Windows suite was not repeated.
verification.native: Refined build passes 14 native Back/reorder/cancellation checks and 8 moved-editor/IME checks in both themes (refined-android-back-cancel and refined-android-editor under out/ux008). After the final pending-edit bulk-notification correction, the exact final APK repeats all 8 accepted row-swipe cases successfully (final-android-swipes). Earlier 14-case check/correction evidence is retained as history; the final bulk edge case is covered by the normal Windows flow suite.
verification.dispatch: Refined emulator VibratorManagerService records all five QShopper effects: 13 GestureEnd, 16 Confirm, 21 ToggleOn, 22 ToggleOff and 25 DragStart. See refined-vibrator-history.txt and refined-native-haptic-summary.json under out/ux008. History confirms dispatch, not physical feel or per-action uniqueness; held-touch request assertions establish timing/uniqueness.
verification.test_fixture: Use the existing activated-window fixture for TouchCancel and verify recovery before ending the synthetic sequence. Fast synthetic moves are compressed by Qt, so the swipe test renders one frame while still held before asserting active recognition and feedback; velocity-only actions still travel less than half width and must succeed. The pending-edit regression reopens its single-row fixture and targets the real editor button without assuming a zero ListView origin.
verification.phone_check: With system Touch feedback enabled: every upward pulley crossing cues. A held swipe cues initially and each time the row crosses centre into the opposite action; same-side pullback stays silent. Shopping check/uncheck and edit delete use Confirm; edit check/uncheck keeps ToggleOn/ToggleOff. Moving rows cue at pickup, each dragged-row index change and normal drop; editor cues on arrival. Displaced rows, no-op taps, startup/reload and cancelled drops stay silent.
verification.phone_report: 2026-11-19: user initially reported no vibration, then confirmed system Touch feedback was off. The View-based API respects that setting, so suppression is expected. No permission or application-code change is justified by this report. Await retest with Touch feedback enabled; successful physical vibration/feel has not yet been confirmed. On 2026-11-20 the user reports an actual pulley cue once per drag and requests a cue on every upward threshold crossing; this establishes that pulley feedback is being felt, not acceptance of all effects or the latest rearming fix.
verification.refinement_before: The prior completion-timed implementation fails the held-finger threshold test: expected one request before release, actual zero (threshold-timing-before.txt). A separate regression reproduces the count-based bulk-delete gap with the only row being edited: actual deletion leaves count unchanged and produces zero versus one expected cue (pending-delete-before-final.txt). Both reports are under out/ux008.
verification.refinement_regressions: The held-threshold regression fails before the timing change and passes after. The pending-only-item Clear-list regression fails before notification-based bulk feedback and passes after, including Undo and no duplicate cues. Final flow suite has 20 passing records (refined-flow-final.txt). Fast-swipe recognition/timing 24, cancellation/pickup/drop 11 and keyboard/Back 14 also pass. Gesture/action logic and ordering remain unchanged.
verification.recross_before: 2026-11-20: revised production-control held-touch regression fails the once-per-drag implementation on the first re-crossing: actual request count 1, expected 2 (out/ux008/recross-before.txt).
verification.recross_after: 2026-11-20: test_mode_pull_threshold passes with three upward crossings in one held drag, silence while staying above/crossing downward, and no extra release/completion cue. Three QtTest records pass (recross-after.txt/xml). Windows app rebuilt; all 74 QML files match the formatter. The full flow/native suites were not repeated for this one-predicate change.
verification.effects_before: Updated control-driven shopping correction expectations fail the previous mapping in both directions (ToggleOn observed instead of Confirm); edit-mode left check/uncheck passes with ToggleOn/ToggleOff. out/ux008/effects-before.txt.
verification.effects_after: Shopping check/uncheck now Confirm in both directions; edit-mode left check/uncheck remains ToggleOn/ToggleOff and right-delete Confirm. Updated correction rows pass (effects-after.txt), swipe matrix 24 passes and cancellation 11 passes (effects-swipes.txt/effects-cancel.txt). These mappings are also retained by the later index-tick focus/cancellation run.
verification.index_tick_before: With actual held-row movement across two indices and a displaced neighbour, prior implementation emits only pickup: 1 request versus 3 expected before drop (out/ux008/index-tick-before.txt).
verification.index_tick_after: The held-row regression observes actual indexChanged notifications from the dragged and displaced rows, requires one SegmentTick per dragged-row change only, then one GestureEnd at drop, preserved order and no restart cue. Eight focused QtTest records pass, including correction mode mapping, repeated pulley crossings and blocked checked-row pickup; cancellation 11 passes (out/ux008/index-tick-after.txt/xml and index-tick-cancel.txt/xml). No full suite repeat.
verification.held_swipes_before: Production touch regression test_repeated_held_swipes fails the activation-only implementation in both modes on the second action side: actual 1 request, expected 2 (out/ux008/held-swipes-before.txt).
verification.held_swipes_after: Shopping/editing held right-left-right sweeps each emit three correctly mapped cues. Same-side partial reversal, release and return animation emit none; sub-threshold gestures preserve items. Swipe suite 26 records and cancellation suite 11 pass (out/ux008/held-swipes-after.txt/xml and held-swipes-cancel.txt/xml). No full/native suite repeat for this QML-only refinement.
